notes: Identity independently confirmed from title page and closing citation: Shanks, Barbieri-Hermitte and Vadillo (2020), Do Incidental Environmental Anchors Bias Consumers’ Price Estimations?, Collabra: Psychology 6(1):19, DOI 10.1525/collabra.310; labelled ORIGINAL RESEARCH REPORT. Supplied canonical text contains all 15 article pages, methods, results, tables and references, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF path supplied; no PDF rendered. Target selected by supplied study identifier, restaurant outcome, and the article’s explicit connection to Critcher and Gilovich Study 3 and Dogerlioglu-Demir and Koçaş Study 1 (p.3 Study 1 aims, p.5 discussion, p.7 Study 3). Business-name wording is interpreted in that explicit original-study context as Studio 97 versus Studio 17, rather than Tap 92 versus Tap 42. Repeated indistinguishable locators receive the same source-supported restaurant test; no assignment by row order or numeric matching. Study 2 locator p.5 introduces its restaurant design; its results are on p.6. Analytic N derivation: 406 + 422 = 828. High and Low are exclusive randomized anchor conditions for the same restaurant item, not repeated observations to be pooled across items. Table 3 Restaurant: Cohen’s d –0.01, t –0.20, df 826, BF+0 0.07. No numerical restaurant p or numerical p bound is printed. All-data exploratory BF+0 0.16 is a different analysis and is not mixed into the primary test. Unassigned original and effect-size fields are placeholders only.
